sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: Today, as a teenager,
sentences.zh: 今天，诺拉·杰克逊在十几岁时，

sentences.en: Nora Jackson was convicted of murder and spent 11 years in prison.
sentences.zh: 被判谋杀罪并入狱服刑了11年。

sentences.en: But from the start, prosecutors possessed a single document that could have set her free.
sentences.zh: 但从一开始，检方就掌握了一份本可以让她重获自由的文件。

sentences.en: Why the omission of evidence, despite its life-altering consequences, is hard to detect and almost never punished.
sentences.zh: 为什么这种证据遗漏尽管后果足以改变人生，却难以察觉且几乎从未受到惩罚。

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月7日，星期一。

sentences.en: Three years ago, in a woman's prison outside Memphis, Tennessee, Nora Jackson was sitting in her cell watching television on mute.
sentences.zh: 三年前，在田纳西州孟菲斯市外的一所女子监狱里，诺拉·杰克逊正坐在牢房里看着静音的电视。

sentences.en: You know, they have 3-1, 3-2, and 3-3, and 3-2 is just like a repeat of the news and the weather.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们有3-1、3-2和3-3频道，3-2频道只是新闻和天气的重播。

sentences.en: Her roommate was in the cafeteria, and Nora wanted to get some privacy.
sentences.zh: 她的室友在食堂，诺拉想拥有一些私人空间。

sentences.en: And I just was sitting there going to the bathroom and just like watching it, and I saw my name come across the bottom of the screen.
sentences.zh: 我当时正坐在那儿，去了一趟洗手间，就像往常一样看着电视，然后我看到我的名字出现在屏幕下方。

sentences.en: And then I was like, oh, shit.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，噢，该死。

sentences.en: So she turns on the volume.
sentences.zh: 于是她打开了音量。

sentences.en: The Tennessee Supreme Court has granted Nora Jackson a new trial.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州最高法院已批准诺拉·杰克逊进行重审。

sentences.en: And she just honestly, for a few minutes, couldn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 老实说，她在那几分钟里简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: Nora Jackson is now awaiting a new trial.
sentences.zh: 诺拉·杰克逊目前正在等待重审。

sentences.en: And even though there's no...
sentences.zh: 尽管还没有……

sentences.en: Nora had just won her appeal, something that rarely happens in the state of Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 诺拉刚刚赢得了上诉，这在田纳西州是很少见的。

sentences.en: This is after she has spent nine years in prison.
sentences.zh: 这是在她入狱九年之后。

sentences.en: Emily Bazelon has been covering the case.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽·巴泽隆一直在报道这个案件。

sentences.en: And like, nobody was there because everybody was at dinner.
sentences.zh: 当时那里没人，因为大家都去吃晚饭了。

sentences.en: So I'm like screaming to get out because I'm like wanting to get to the phone, and nobody's there.
sentences.zh: 所以我大声尖叫着想出去，因为我想去打电话，但没人应答。

sentences.en: It must have been something good to eat that night.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上一定吃了什么好东西。

sentences.en: And why was Nora in prison in the first place?
sentences.zh: 那么诺拉最初为什么会入狱呢？

sentences.en: Nora was in prison because she was convicted of murdering her mother, Jennifer Jackson.
sentences.zh: 诺拉入狱是因为她被判谋杀了自己的母亲詹妮弗·杰克逊。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: On the night of September 4th, 2005, Nora Jackson was out all night.
sentences.zh: 2005年9月4日晚上，诺拉·杰克逊整晚都在外面。

sentences.en: She was at a couple of parties with some friends.
sentences.zh: 她和朋友们参加了几个聚会。

sentences.en: Then she later said that she was driving around.
sentences.zh: 后来她说自己一直在开车兜风。

sentences.en: And that same night, in the very early morning hours, her mother was brutally stabbed to death in their home.
sentences.zh: 就在那天晚上，也就是凌晨时分，她的母亲在家里被残忍地刺死。

sentences.en: Fire Department, what's the address of your emergency?
sentences.zh: 消防局，请问您的紧急情况地址在哪里？

sentences.en: I mean, it's 5,001 New Haven Avenue.
sentences.zh: 我是说，地址是纽黑文大道5001号。

sentences.en: What's the problem with them exactly what happened?
sentences.zh: 他们到底出了什么问题，发生了什么事？

sentences.en: No, because it's in my house.
sentences.zh: 不，因为是在我家。

sentences.en: My mom, because my mom is bleeding.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈，因为我妈妈在流血。

sentences.en: Is she breathing?
sentences.zh: 她还在呼吸吗？

sentences.en: No, she's not breathing.
sentences.zh: 不，她没有呼吸了。

sentences.en: She's not breathing.
sentences.zh: 她没有呼吸了。

sentences.en: She's not breathing.
sentences.zh: 她没有呼吸了。

sentences.en: She was stabbed to death 50 times.
sentences.zh: 她被刺了50刀身亡。

sentences.en: Please send an ambulance, please send an ambulance.
sentences.zh: 请派救护车，请派救护车。

sentences.en: Okay, listen.
sentences.zh: 好的，听着。

sentences.en: Please send an ambulance.
sentences.zh: 请派救护车。

sentences.en: We have help on the way.
sentences.zh: 救援人员正在赶往现场。

sentences.en: We're going to help your mother.
sentences.zh: 我们会救你母亲的。

sentences.en: As the yellow tape goes up on Jennifer Jackson's front lawn, theories of her murder start blooming like Tennessee passion flowers.
sentences.zh: 当詹妮弗·杰克逊家前草坪拉起警戒线时，关于她谋杀案的各种理论就像田纳西州的西番莲一样层出不穷。

sentences.en: There were TV reports about it calling it an unsolved, mysterious stabbing.
sentences.zh: 电视报道称这是一起未破的神秘刺杀案。

sentences.en: Police calling Jackson's murder a home invasion, robbery, homicide.
sentences.zh: 警方称杰克逊的谋杀案是一起入室抢劫杀人案。

sentences.en: Maybe it's a robbery gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 也许是一起抢劫未遂导致的悲剧。

sentences.en: So, Emily, then what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, then Amy Wyrick got the file.
sentences.zh: 嗯，后来艾米·怀里克接手了这个案卷。

sentences.en: Anyone who thought Shelby County's first female DA would be a pushover, well, they don't know Amy Wyrick.
sentences.zh: 任何认为谢尔比县首位女性地方检察官会好欺负的人，那他们就不了解艾米·怀里克。

sentences.en: And Amy Wyrick was a rising star in the Memphis courthouse.
sentences.zh: 艾米·怀里克是孟菲斯法院的一颗冉冉升起的新星。

sentences.en: She was known as a formidable child lawyer.
sentences.zh: 她以一名强硬的青少年律师而闻名。

sentences.en: As a prosecutor for over 20 years, I have worked hard every day to make sure those who break the law are held accountable.
sentences.zh: 作为一名检察官，二十多年来，我每天都在努力工作，确保那些违法者受到法律的制裁。

sentences.en: I'm Amy Wyrick.
sentences.zh: 我是艾米·怀里克。

sentences.en: I'm a prosecutor, but I'm also a mother.
sentences.zh: 我是一名检察官，但我也是一位母亲。

sentences.en: And I'll go after anyone who threatens our community.
sentences.zh: 我会追究任何威胁我们社区的人。

sentences.en: And Nora's case went to her.
sentences.zh: 诺拉的案子交到了她手里。

sentences.en: Amy Wyrick developed a theory.
sentences.zh: 艾米·怀里克提出了一个理论。

sentences.en: She thought that Nora had killed her mother for money because she, Nora, wanted to keep a kind of partying lifestyle going.
sentences.zh: 她认为诺拉为了钱杀害了母亲，因为诺拉想继续维持那种派对生活方式。

sentences.en: Nora, at this point, was 18.
sentences.zh: 当时诺拉18岁。

sentences.en: She'd been having some trouble in school.
sentences.zh: 她在学校里遇到了一些麻烦。

sentences.en: And Wyrick thought that Nora's mother was setting down rules that Nora didn't like and that they were clashing over money.
sentences.zh: 怀里克认为诺拉的母亲制定了诺拉不喜欢的规矩，她们在金钱问题上发生了冲突。

sentences.en: That's a pretty significant theory to have developed.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当重大的推论。

sentences.en: Did the prosecutor have any evidence to suggest that?
sentences.zh: 检察官有任何证据支持这一点吗？

sentences.en: There are a couple of hours in the middle of the night when Nora was unaccounted for.
sentences.zh: 在深夜里有几个小时诺拉的行踪不明。

sentences.en: She wasn't calling anyone or texting anyone.
sentences.zh: 她没有给任何人打电话或发短信。

sentences.en: And she had a cut on her hand.
sentences.zh: 而且她的手上有一道伤口。

sentences.en: Nora's family members and friends of hers said that she had given differing explanations for this cut.
sentences.zh: 诺拉的家人和朋友说，她对这道伤口给出了不同的解释。

sentences.en: And so all of that loomed very large at child.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切在审判中显得非常重要。

sentences.en: She took those knives with premeditation, thinking of one thing.
sentences.zh: 她带着那些刀具，预谋着，心里只想着一件事。

sentences.en: She wasn't going to cut baloney with those knives.
sentences.zh: 她拿那些刀可不是为了切午餐肉。

sentences.en: She was going to cut the thing that was standing in the way of her lifestyle of freedom.
sentences.zh: 她要切断的是阻碍她追求自由生活方式的障碍。

sentences.en: Another key piece of the puzzle from the point of view of the prosecution was a witness named Andrew Hammock.
sentences.zh: 从检方的角度来看，拼图的另一个关键部分是一位名叫安德鲁·哈莫克的证人。

sentences.en: Throughout the night and the last thing, I do remember when I woke up, I had a text message or a voicemail that said answer.
sentences.zh: 整晚以及最后，我记得当我醒来时，有一条短信或语音留言说接电话。

sentences.en: And he testified at trial that she called him somewhere between 4 and 5 in the morning and asked him to meet her at her house.
sentences.zh: 他在庭审中作证说，她在凌晨4点到5点之间给他打了电话，并要求他在她家见面。

sentences.en: And so he became a critical witness because he was the only person who placed Nora at the scene of the murder.
sentences.zh: 因此他成为了一个关键证人，因为他是唯一一个将诺拉置于谋杀现场的人。

sentences.en: Just tell us where you were.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你在哪里。

sentences.en: That's all we're asking, Nora.
sentences.zh: 诺拉，我们要求的仅此而已。

sentences.en: The jury deliberated for nine hours and they came back into the courtroom.
sentences.zh: 陪审团商议了九个小时，然后回到了法庭。

sentences.en: And Nora says she remembered that she tried to make eye contact with some of the jurors and none of them would look at her.
sentences.zh: 诺拉说她记得自己试图与一些陪审员进行眼神交流，但他们都没有看她。

sentences.en: And then she heard the verdict.
sentences.zh: 然后她听到了判决结果。

sentences.en: Stand, please, Ms. Jackson.
sentences.zh: 请起立，杰克逊小姐。

sentences.en: Ms. Jackson, upon a jury of your peers having found you guilty of murder in the second degree,
sentences.zh: 杰克逊小姐，鉴于你的同侪陪审团已裁定你犯有二级谋杀罪，

sentences.en: suggesting the court you found guilty of that offense since the 20 years and nine months in the Tennessee Department of Correction as a 100 percent violent offender without parole.
sentences.zh: 建议法庭判处你犯有该罪行，在田纳西州惩教署服刑20年零9个月，作为一名100%的暴力罪犯，不得假释。

sentences.en: And nothing will ever bring Jennifer back to us.
sentences.zh: 没有什么能把詹妮弗带回我们身边。

sentences.en: No amount of time will enable us to comprehend the brutal massacre of our beloved Jennifer by the daughter she loved most in the world.
sentences.zh: 无论多少时间都无法让我们理解，我们挚爱的詹妮弗竟被她在这个世界上最爱的女儿残忍杀害。

sentences.en: So why did Nora appeal this verdict?
sentences.zh: 那么诺拉为什么要对这个判决提出上诉呢？

sentences.en: Andrew Hammock, this key witness, had written a note to the police that the prosecutors should have turned over to the defense and did not.
sentences.zh: 关键证人安德鲁·哈莫克曾写过一张纸条给警方，检方本应将其移交给辩方，但却没有这样做。

sentences.en: And one of the things it said was that Andrew Hammock was rolling on ecstasy the night of the murder.
sentences.zh: 其中提到的一点是，安德鲁·哈莫克在谋杀当晚服用了摇头丸。

sentences.en: And then the other thing he said was that he had left his phone with his friend Ian.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是他提到把手机留给了朋友伊恩。

sentences.en: And the reason that that was important was that his testimony, obviously, was about this idea that Nora had called him and that he had actually spoken to Nora.
sentences.zh: 这一点之所以重要，是因为他的证词显然是关于诺拉给他打了电话，而且他确实与诺拉通过话。

sentences.en: And so if Andrew Hammock didn't actually have his phone at this key part of the night, then it seems like he couldn't have talked to Nora.
sentences.zh: 所以如果安德鲁·哈莫克在当晚这个关键时刻并没有手机，那么他似乎不可能与诺拉通过话。

sentences.en: And legally, Emily, why is the existence of this note and how it was treated so important?
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，从法律上讲，这张纸条的存在及其处理方式为什么如此重要？

sentences.en: Everyone who's accused of a crime before a trial has the right to all the evidence the state has collected that is favorable to them and material to their guilt or innocence.
sentences.zh: 每个在审判前被指控犯罪的人，都有权获得国家收集的、对他们有利且对定罪或无罪至关重要的所有证据。

sentences.en: And when you step back and think about this for a minute, the reason is that the state, the prosecution has on its side the police and the crime labs,
sentences.zh: 当你退后一步思考一下，原因在于国家和检方拥有警方和犯罪实验室作为后盾，

sentences.en: all the kind of investigative muscle of the government.
sentences.zh: 拥有政府所有的调查力量。

sentences.en: And so because of all of that power that that gives the state, we have this rule.
sentences.zh: 正是因为这种赋予国家的力量，我们才有了这条规则。

sentences.en: It comes from a 1963 Supreme Court case called Brady v.
sentences.zh: 它源于1963年最高法院的一个案件，名为布雷迪诉

sentences.en: Maryland.
sentences.zh: 马里兰州案。

sentences.en: John Leo Brady was on death row in Maryland in 1963.
sentences.zh: 约翰·里奥·布雷迪在1963年时在马里兰州死囚牢房中。

sentences.en: And when his lawyers appealed, they found out that a co-defendant had confessed to the killing that he was on death row for.
sentences.zh: 当他的律师上诉时，他们发现一名共同被告承认了导致他入狱的谋杀罪。

sentences.en: And the prosecutors knew that at his trial, and they never told the jury, and they never told the defense.
sentences.zh: 检察官在审判时知道这一点，但他们从未告诉陪审团，也从未告诉辩方。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court thought, you know what, this is a really important piece of information
sentences.zh: 最高法院认为，你知道吗，这是一个非常重要的信息，

sentences.en: that should have been disclosed to the defense beforehand so the defense could have brought it up and used it at the trial.
sentences.zh: 本应事先披露给辩方，以便辩方可以在审判中提出并使用它。

sentences.en: And so what we're really talking about here fundamentally is kind of balancing the scales or trying to even the scales between the prosecution and the defense.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里真正讨论的，从根本上说是平衡天平，或者说是试图拉平检方与辩方之间的差距。

sentences.en: So 1963 makes this a pretty recent development in American criminal justice.
sentences.zh: 所以1963年使这成为美国刑事司法中一个相当近期的发展。

sentences.en: Did the prosecution not have to hand over evidence that's material and favorable before that time?
sentences.zh: 在此之前，检方不需要移交实质性且有利的证据吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The prosecution did not have an obligation in the United States to hand over any evidence at all, at least not a constitutional obligation.
sentences.zh: 在美国，检方没有义务移交任何证据，至少没有宪法义务。

sentences.en: And the idea was that there was going to be an element of surprise.
sentences.zh: 当时的理念是会存在一种突袭的成分。

sentences.en: You didn't even find out what you were charged with until the trial.
sentences.zh: 你甚至直到审判时才知道自己被指控了什么。

sentences.en: And the surprise was to help ascertain the truth.
sentences.zh: 而这种突袭是为了帮助查明真相。

sentences.en: That was the idea, that people would answer in the moment, and the jury or the judge would be able to tell whether they were telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时的理念，人们会当场回答，陪审团或法官就能判断他们是否在说真话。

sentences.en: Trial by ambush.
sentences.zh: 伏击式审判。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is the sort of cinematic version of criminal justice, where the lawyer tells the person on the stand, you know, how do you explain this?
sentences.zh: 这是刑事司法的电影版本，律师问证人席上的人，你知道，你怎么解释这个？

sentences.en: And it feels like actually that's been illegal for quite some time.
sentences.zh: 感觉这实际上已经非法很久了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're talking about something that the defense should have had, that they should have been able to prepare for and react to,
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是辩方本应拥有的东西，他们本应能够为此做好准备并做出反应，

sentences.en: and that the jury and the judge also should have found out about.
sentences.zh: 而且陪审团和法官也本应了解到的情况。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So back to Nora Jackson.
sentences.zh: 回到诺拉·杰克逊的案子。

sentences.en: What is the explanation for why this note was not shared with the defense?
sentences.zh: 关于为什么这张纸条没有与辩方分享，有什么解释吗？

sentences.en: The assistant prosecutor at the trial, whose name's Stephen Jones, said that he got the note in the middle of the trial.
sentences.zh: 审判时的助理检察官斯蒂芬·琼斯说，他在审判过程中收到了这张纸条。

sentences.en: He read it, and then he put it in a flap of his trial notebook, intending to turn it over to the defense, but then he forgot about it.
sentences.zh: 他读了它，然后把它放在了审判笔记本的夹层里，打算交给辩方，但后来他忘了。

sentences.en: So he says this was an innocent mistake.
sentences.zh: 所以他说这是一个无心的错误。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So basically, like, lost it within his own filing system.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上就是，在他自己的归档系统中弄丢了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then came upon it after the trial was over, and at that point, several days after the guilty verdict, he filed a motion calling attention to it as omitted evidence
sentences.zh: 后来在审判结束后发现了它，当时在有罪判决几天后，他提交了一份动议，提请注意这是遗漏的证据，

sentences.en: and turning it over to the judge.
sentences.zh: 并将其移交给了法官。

sentences.en: Don't you emcee?
sentences.zh: 你不主持吗？

sentences.en: Action News 5 at 10.
sentences.zh: 10点档行动新闻5台。

sentences.en: Starts now.
sentences.zh: 现在开始。

sentences.en: But the trial judge did not grant Nora a new trial based on this new piece of evidence, and so the case traveled all the way up on appeal to the Tennessee Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 但主审法官并没有基于这一新证据批准诺拉重审，因此案件一路上诉到了田纳西州最高法院。

sentences.en: Now, the Shelby County District Attorney General Amy Weirich in the hot seat after courtroom mistakes, according to some, help a convicted mother killer get a new trial.
sentences.zh: 现在，谢尔比县地方检察长艾米·怀里克因庭审失误而处于风口浪尖，据一些人称，这些失误帮助了一名被判杀母罪的女子获得了重审机会。

sentences.en: It's been a busy night of breaking news in the Mid-South.
sentences.zh: 今晚是中南地区突发新闻繁忙的一夜。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: I'm Joe Birch.
sentences.zh: 我是乔·伯奇。

sentences.en: The Tennessee Supreme Court has ordered a new trial for Nora Jackson.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州最高法院已下令对诺拉·杰克逊进行重审。

sentences.en: Jackson's attorney, Valerie Quarter, says her client should have never been convicted.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊的律师瓦莱丽·夸特表示，她的当事人本不该被定罪。

sentences.en: Quarter says investigators linked Jackson to the murder with little physical evidence.
sentences.zh: 夸特说，调查人员在几乎没有物证的情况下将杰克逊与这起谋杀案联系了起来。

sentences.en: There was circumstantial evidence against Nora, but the DNA analysis in this case points away from Nora.
sentences.zh: 针对诺拉的确实有间接证据，但本案的 DNA 分析结果却排除了诺拉的嫌疑。

sentences.en: It excluded her as being one of the people whose blood was found at the scene of the crime and pointed to other unknown suspects.
sentences.zh: 分析结果排除了她是案发现场血迹来源的可能性，并指向了其他身份不明的嫌疑人。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a big part of this case, and so the Tennessee Supreme Court, looking at that, thought, well, given the lack of physical evidence
sentences.zh: 是的，这是本案的关键点，所以田纳西州最高法院在审视这一点时认为，鉴于缺乏物证，

sentences.en: and these DNA results, that makes the testimony of this single witness, Andrew Hammack, who puts Nora at the scene of the crime, really important.
sentences.zh: 再加上这些 DNA 检测结果，使得那位将诺拉置于案发现场的唯一证人安德鲁·哈马克的证词变得至关重要。

sentences.en: Did you talk to the lead prosecutor, Amy Weirich, about the possibility that this could have been a turning point in the case, this failure, to disclose that letter?
sentences.zh: 你有没有和首席检察官艾米·韦里奇谈过，关于这封信未披露的失误是否可能成为案件转折点的问题？

sentences.en: I just turned on my tape recorder.
sentences.zh: 我刚打开录音机。

sentences.en: Yes, I did talk to her about that in an interview, and she really dismisses that possibility.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在采访中确实和她谈过这个问题，但她完全否认了这种可能性。

sentences.en: I found out about the missing statement
sentences.zh: 我是在史蒂夫·琼斯发现那份缺失的陈述之后，

sentences.en: sometime after Steve Jones discovered it.
sentences.zh: 才得知此事的。

sentences.en: Right, but like, when?
sentences.zh: 没错，但具体是什么时候？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我毫无头绪。

sentences.en: And then when he realized he had forgotten, he told me that, and Steve did what every prosecutor in the country would do.
sentences.zh: 后来当他意识到自己忘了这件事时，他告诉了我，而史蒂夫做了全国任何检察官都会做的事。

sentences.en: He reported it to the judge, and he put it in the hands of the judge to handle.
sentences.zh: 他向法官报告了此事，并交由法官处理。

sentences.en: So you don't remember that moment when he told you about that?
sentences.zh: 所以你不记得他告诉你这件事的那一刻了？

sentences.en: And I guess the reason I'm asking is that, you know, potentially, and in fact this happened, like, that note turned into a Brady violation that led to a reversal of the conviction.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这么问，是因为实际上确实发生了这种情况，那张便条演变成了一起违反《布雷迪规则》的行为，导致定罪被撤销。

sentences.en: So I just imagine that it might be kind of memorable.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这应该挺让人印象深刻的。

sentences.en: Well, you might imagine that it would be, but it's not, because I think that illustrates how uncertain the world of Brady has become.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能觉得会是这样，但事实并非如此，因为我认为这恰恰说明了《布雷迪规则》的适用环境已经变得多么不确定。

sentences.en: This was a trial that took two weeks.
sentences.zh: 那是一场持续了两周的审判。

sentences.en: This was a trial with 40-something witnesses.
sentences.zh: 那是一场有四十多位证人的审判。

sentences.en: This was a trial with 400 pieces of evidence.
sentences.zh: 那是一场有四百件证据的审判。

sentences.en: And yes, it happened.
sentences.zh: 是的，事情确实发生了。

sentences.en: And yes, the case was reversed because of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，案件也确实因此被推翻了。

sentences.en: But, um, lessons learned.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，吸取教训吧。

sentences.en: Um, so you were talking earlier, I think you said that the...
sentences.zh: 嗯，你刚才在谈论时，我想你说的是……

sentences.en: I've got to wrap up.
sentences.zh: 我得结束了。

sentences.en: I've got to...
sentences.zh: 我得……

sentences.en: Okay, let me just ask you two more questions.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我再问你两个问题。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，而且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载应用程序，获取 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Emily, you've been studying this one case, but how often do you think this happens where an omission of evidence, by accident or deliberately,
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，你一直在研究这个案子，你认为这种因意外或蓄意隐瞒证据而导致……

sentences.en: sways the outcome of a case?
sentences.zh: 左右案件结果的情况，发生的频率有多高？

sentences.en: You know, it's really hard to answer the question of how often prosecutors fail to disclose evidence because we're talking about something that's hidden.
sentences.zh: 你知道，要回答检察官隐瞒证据的频率有多高真的很难，因为我们讨论的是隐藏起来的事情。

sentences.en: It's hard to know whether we can be sure that it ever comes to light.
sentences.zh: 很难确定我们是否能确信这些隐瞒行为终会大白于天下。

sentences.en: But there are some telling studies.
sentences.zh: 但有一些研究很有说明力。

sentences.en: One of them was conducted in 2002 by a couple of Columbia Law School professors, and they reviewed 2,700 death sentences across the country.
sentences.zh: 其中一项研究是 2002 年由两位哥伦比亚大学法学院教授进行的，他们审查了全国 2700 起死刑判决。

sentences.en: And what these law professors were saying was that their analysis showed that it was in close cases, those in which a small amount of evidence
sentences.zh: 这些法学教授指出，他们的分析显示，在那些证据较少、

sentences.en: might tip the outcome in a different direction, that the risk of serious error is the greateSt.
sentences.zh: 可能左右判决结果的胶着案件中，出现严重错误的风险最大。

sentences.en: And that's a pretty chilling possibility, the idea that it might be more likely for evidence to be withheld when proof of guilt is uncertain.
sentences.zh: 这是一种相当令人不寒而栗的可能性，即在罪证不确凿时，证据被隐瞒的可能性反而更大。

sentences.en: Why I chose to be a prosecutor?
sentences.zh: 我为什么选择当检察官？

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: To do justice.
sentences.zh: 为了伸张正义。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: The court system appealed to me.
sentences.zh: 法院系统吸引了我。

sentences.en: Trying cases to a jury appealed to me.
sentences.zh: 在陪审团面前进行庭审吸引了我。

sentences.en: Being on the side of doing the right thing every day for the right reason.
sentences.zh: 站在每天为了正当理由做正确事情的一方。

sentences.en: I can't think of a better way to use a law license.
sentences.zh: 我想不出比这更好的利用律师执照的方式了。

sentences.en: You know, prosecutors have this difficult dual role they play.
sentences.zh: 你知道，检察官扮演着一种艰难的双重角色。

sentences.en: It's their job to win convictions, and it's also their job to be ministers of justice.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作既是赢得定罪，也是担任正义的维护者。

sentences.en: In other words, they have a kind of broader responsibility to fairness.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们对公平负有更广泛的责任。

sentences.en: Sometimes those roles are in tension, and if you have an office where the message is one that really values winning above all else, you can kind of throw that balance out of whack.
sentences.zh: 有时这些角色会产生冲突，如果你所在的办公室传达的信息是把胜诉看得高于一切，那么这种平衡就会被打破。

sentences.en: So one thing that some of the experts I talked to mentioned as a potential red flag is that in Shelby County for a long time there's been something called a Hammer Award,
sentences.zh: 我采访的一些专家提到的一个潜在危险信号是，在谢尔比县长期以来一直存在所谓的“铁锤奖”，

sentences.en: where if you win a case or you get a big sentence, you get this award with a picture of a hammer.
sentences.zh: 如果你赢了一场官司或获得重判，就会得到这个印有锤子图案的奖项。

sentences.en: A Hammer Award?
sentences.zh: 铁锤奖？

sentences.en: That was something that was started
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前，

sentences.en: a million years ago by an assistant who is now deceased.
sentences.zh: 由一位现已去世的助理检察官发起的。

sentences.en: And he would take those on people's doors after they got a verdict.
sentences.zh: 他们在获得判决后会把奖贴在人们的门上。

sentences.en: Just a way to let the office know.
sentences.zh: 这只是让办公室知道的一种方式。

sentences.en: This was, you know, before emails and everything else, to let the office know that a trial was over, and that was the verdict.
sentences.zh: 这还是在电子邮件和其他通讯手段普及之前，用来告知办公室审判结束以及判决结果的方式。

sentences.en: Are there any other ways of recognizing merit that the office has?
sentences.zh: 办公室还有其他认可功绩的方式吗？

sentences.en: Like if you dismiss a case and that was the right thing to do, is there a way to recognize that?
sentences.zh: 比如如果你撤销了一起案件，而这又是正确的做法，有办法认可这一点吗？

sentences.en: Of course there is.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: Quite frankly, we dismiss more cases around here than we actually get convictions on.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我们撤销的案件比实际获得定罪的案件还要多。

sentences.en: Why we don't keep up with conviction rates and things like that, because that's not our job.
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不追踪定罪率之类的指标，因为那不是我们的工作。

sentences.en: Our job is to do justice.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作是伸张正义。

sentences.en: And sometimes that justice is going to trial and presenting the best case you can and putting it in the hands of the jury.
sentences.zh: 有时正义意味着进行审判，尽可能呈现最好的证据，并将其交给陪审团裁决。

sentences.en: And oftentimes that justice is dismissing charges.
sentences.zh: 而很多时候，正义意味着撤销指控。

sentences.en: You know, one thing that was sort of surprising to me was when I looked at this office back in time, there have been a number of issues about failure to disclose evidence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一件事让我感到惊讶，当我回顾这个办公室的历史时，发现曾多次出现未披露证据的问题。

sentences.en: I should also add that some of the allegations against this office and failing to disclose evidence involve Amy Weirich herself and a couple of other cases.
sentences.zh: 我还应该补充一点，针对该办公室的一些指控，以及未能披露证据的问题，也涉及艾米·韦里奇本人和其他几起案件。

sentences.en: There's this kind of mysterious disappeared envelope in an old case.
sentences.zh: 在旧案中有一个神秘消失的信封。

sentences.en: And I assume that that envelope contained evidence?
sentences.zh: 我猜那个信封里装的是证据？

sentences.en: Well, it's a weird story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个奇怪的故事。

sentences.en: So the new defense attorney and a new prosecutor went back to these old files and they both say they saw a manila envelope that had a yellow sticky on it that said something like,
sentences.zh: 当时新的辩护律师和新的检察官回去查看这些旧档案，他们都说看到一个马尼拉纸信封，上面贴着一张黄色便条，写着类似：

sentences.en: do not turn over to the defense with Amy Weirich's initials.
sentences.zh: “不要交给辩方”，并有艾米·韦里奇的缩写。

sentences.en: And when they went back, they said that that envelope and that sticky note were gone.
sentences.zh: 当他们再次回去时，他们说那个信封和便条都不见了。

sentences.en: Now, Amy Weirich had to give testimony about this.
sentences.zh: 后来，艾米·韦里奇不得不就此事作证。

sentences.en: She denied knowing anything about it in court.
sentences.zh: 她在法庭上否认对此事知情。

sentences.en: And the judge who heard this appeal found that there was no reason to grant the defendant a new trial.
sentences.zh: 而审理此上诉案的法官认为没有理由给予被告重审的机会。

sentences.en: That order is now on appeal.
sentences.zh: 该裁决目前正在上诉中。

sentences.en: But these accusations have been coming up in multiple cases in Shelby County.
sentences.zh: 但这些指控在谢尔比县的多起案件中不断出现。

sentences.en: Prosecutors are not perfect.
sentences.zh: 检察官并非完美无缺。

sentences.en: This office touches over 200,000 cases every year and mistakes are going to be made.
sentences.zh: 这个办公室每年处理超过 20 万起案件，难免会犯错。

sentences.en: But there is a huge difference between a mistake and misconduct.
sentences.zh: 但错误和不当行为之间有着巨大的区别。

sentences.en: You were talking earlier about Jennifer Jackson, you know, how the Hammock statement didn't point to someone else believing someone else killing Jennifer Jackson.
sentences.zh: 你刚才谈到了詹妮弗·杰克逊，关于哈马克的陈述并没有指向其他人相信是别人杀了詹妮弗·杰克逊。

sentences.en: So when you learned of the DNA results in that case after Nora Jackson was indicted, what did you think about that?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你在诺拉·杰克逊被起诉后得知该案的 DNA 检测结果时，你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: Because those DNA results obviously didn't point to Nora Jackson as the killer.
sentences.zh: 因为那些 DNA 结果显然没有指向诺拉·杰克逊是凶手。

sentences.en: They didn't point to anything as DNA often doesn't.
sentences.zh: 它们没有指向任何人，DNA 检测往往就是这样。

sentences.en: Sometimes DNA is very helpful in eliminating suspects.
sentences.zh: 有时 DNA 在排除嫌疑人方面非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Sometimes DNA is very helpful in identifying suspects.
sentences.zh: 有时 DNA 在识别嫌疑人方面非常有帮助。

sentences.en: But we had a mountain of circumstantial evidence that put the defendant in that home killing her mother at the time lying about it every chance she got afterward
sentences.zh: 但我们有堆积如山的间接证据，证明被告当时就在家中杀害了她的母亲，事后还抓住一切机会撒谎，

sentences.en: destroying and disposing of clothing that she had been wearing earlier in the evening.
sentences.zh: 并销毁和丢弃了她当晚穿过的衣服。

sentences.en: We had motive.
sentences.zh: 我们有动机。

sentences.en: We had everything you can have in a case except for direct DNA evidence.
sentences.zh: 除了直接的 DNA 证据外，我们在案件中拥有了一切。

sentences.en: So when you got that DNA and it was not Nora that didn't make you hesitate?
sentences.zh: 所以当你拿到 DNA 结果发现不是诺拉时，这没让你犹豫过吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: A lot of district attorneys' offices around the country and a whole bunch of states have passed laws in which they've just taken out this whole honor system part of
sentences.zh: 全国各地的许多地方检察官办公室和许多州已经通过了法律，他们取消了这种完全依赖自觉的制度，

sentences.en: whether you disclose evidence or not.
sentences.zh: 即是否披露证据全凭自觉。

sentences.en: Instead of prosecutors trying to make these difficult judgment calls about what's favorable to the defense and what's material, they just open up their files.
sentences.zh: 检察官不再需要费力去判断哪些对辩方有利、哪些是实质性证据，他们直接公开档案。

sentences.en: They say to the defense lawyer, come on in, you look at everything, you know, you decide what's going to help your case.
sentences.zh: 他们对辩护律师说，进来吧，看所有的东西，你自己决定什么对你的案子有帮助。

sentences.en: And so what that suggests to me is that this is one more way in which the quality of justice in the United States really depends on where you are.
sentences.zh: 这向我表明，美国的司法质量在很大程度上取决于你身处何地。

sentences.en: If you're accused of a crime, the state and even the town that you're in can really determine the quality of justice you receive.
sentences.zh: 如果你被指控犯罪，你所在的州甚至你所在的城镇，真的可以决定你所获得的司法质量。

sentences.en: And this brings us back to
sentences.zh: 这让我们回到了

sentences.en: Nora Jackson's prison cell when she found out she had won her appeal and that her conviction had been overturned.
sentences.zh: 诺拉·杰克逊的牢房，当时她得知上诉成功，定罪被撤销了。

sentences.en: What happened next to her?
sentences.zh: 她后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: So Nora Jackson had kind of a hard road.
sentences.zh: 诺拉·杰克逊走过了一段艰难的路。

sentences.en: That was an exciting day.
sentences.zh: 那是个令人兴奋的日子。

sentences.en: She knew that she was going to get another chance and there was a fight going on where her lawyers were trying to get
sentences.zh: 她知道自己会得到另一次机会，当时她的律师正在努力争取

sentences.en: Amy Weirich and her office removed from the case.
sentences.zh: 将艾米·韦里奇及其办公室从案件中撤换掉。

sentences.en: Eventually the judge did appoint a new prosecutor and he offered
sentences.zh: 最终法官确实任命了一位新的检察官，他向

sentences.en: Nora Jackson a deal.
sentences.zh: 诺拉·杰克逊提供了一项协议。

sentences.en: He said if you plead to voluntary manslaughter
sentences.zh: 他说如果你承认过失杀人罪，
